title: observability: token-level metrics + tracing + dashboards + alert tuning
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation: We need token-level observability (metrics + tracing + dashboards) to understand per-token cost/latency behavior and KV-cache effectiveness across workloads. This PR implements token-level metrics (per-request token counters and cost attribution), enriches tracing spans with token metadata, ships new dashboards for token-level cost/latency breakdowns, and adjusts alert thresholds to reduce noisy paging while preserving SLO coverage.

Changes included (high-level):
- Introduced token-level metrics: token_count.total, token_count.generated, token_count.prompt, token_cost. Metrics tag by model, route, customer_tier, cache_hit (true/false) and seq_len_bucket.
- KV cache metrics: kv_cache.hits, kv_cache.misses, kv_cache.hit_ratio (per-model & per-route). Added kv_cache.latency histogram.
- Tracing: added span attributes span.token_count, span.kv_cache_hits, span.kv_cache_miss, span.seq_len. Propagated model_variant tags for easier rollups.
- Dashboards: new Token Level Cost/Latency dashboard (console/dashboards/token_level.yml) with cost breakdown by token position, cache-hit overlays, and per-model heatmaps.
- Alerts: tuned token-cost and latency alerts to use median and 95th percentile bucketing by seq_len_bucket and ignore short-lived spikes from cold starts. Adjusted alert thresholds to reduce noise; added longer evaluation windows for P99 on dedicated customers.
- Tests: added integration tests that assert metrics/tags emitted and end-to-end dashboard panels render with expected metrics (testing targets in observability_test.go).
- Docs: updated observability.md with guidance on interpreting token-level metrics and recommended alert configurations.

Checklist:
- [x] Token metrics instrumentation added and covered by unit tests
- [x] Tracing changes implemented and validated in staging traces
- [x] Dashboards committed and smoke-tested in staging Console
- [x] Alerts tuned and validated with synthetic load tests
- [x] Documentation updated

Related: ENG-4273 (token-level telemetry), ENG-4301 (kv-cache metrics), SUP-987 (customer incident that motivated alert tuning).

Rollout plan: feature gated behind env REDWOOD_TOKEN_OBS=true. Rollout will be staged: enable in staging -> enable for 10% of traffic in dedicated -> full rollout. Dashboard panels are additive and read-only. Alerts will be deployed in parallel but set to Notify:dev for 24 hours before Pager escalation.

Notes: This PR is intentionally additive; no backward-incompatible metric renames. Alert tuning may require follow-up after two weeks of telemetry to adjust thresholds for high-volume customers.
